name: PulseBoard
pitch: A real-time analytics dashboard for tracking campaign performance metrics across Adobe Experience Cloud.
description:
PulseBoard aggregates data from multiple Adobe Experience Cloud sources to give marketers a unified view of campaign performance. The dashboard features real-time updates via WebSocket connections, customizable widget layouts, and automated anomaly detection that alerts teams when metrics deviate from expected ranges.

The team built a modular architecture that allows new data sources to be plugged in without modifying the core dashboard logic. This required designing a robust adapter pattern and implementing efficient data transformation pipelines.

PulseBoard was presented at Demo Day and received praise for its intuitive interface and the speed at which it processes large datasets. The project is now being evaluated for integration into an internal analytics toolset.
learnings: We learned that real-time data pipelines are harder than they look — caching strategies and WebSocket connection management were our biggest challenges. User testing with actual PMs changed our entire dashboard layout. The biggest takeaway: always prototype with real data, not mocks.

name: DesignLint
pitch: An automated design consistency checker that audits Figma files against Adobe's design system guidelines.
description:
DesignLint is a Figma plugin that automatically scans design files for inconsistencies with Adobe Spectrum design system guidelines. It checks spacing, color usage, typography hierarchy, component naming conventions, and accessibility contrast ratios.

The plugin generates a detailed report with severity levels, inline annotations pointing to exact violations, and one-click fix suggestions for common issues. It integrates with Jira to automatically create tickets for design debt.

DesignLint won the 'Most Impactful' award at Demo Day for its potential to save hundreds of design review hours across the organization.
learnings: Building a Figma plugin taught us the importance of working within platform constraints. We initially tried to do too much client-side and had to refactor to use Figma's sandbox model. The lesson: understand your platform's architecture before designing your solution.

name: JourneyViz
pitch: An interactive 3D visualization tool for mapping and analyzing customer journey touchpoints.
description:
JourneyViz transforms complex customer journey data into intuitive 3D visualizations. Users can explore touchpoint clusters, identify drop-off patterns, and discover hidden correlations between different journey stages.

The tool uses force-directed graph algorithms to automatically layout journey nodes, with GPU-accelerated rendering via Three.js for smooth interaction even with datasets containing thousands of touchpoints.

The Python backend processes raw event data from Adobe Analytics and generates optimized graph structures for the frontend. A custom caching layer ensures sub-second response times for repeat queries.
learnings: 3D visualization is a double-edged sword — it looks incredible but can be confusing if not designed carefully. We spent two weeks on user testing to find the right balance between visual impact and clarity. Key insight: 3D works best for exploration, but 2D is better for precise analysis.

name: WorkflowForge
pitch: A drag-and-drop workflow builder for automating project management processes in Workfront.
description:
WorkflowForge allows project managers to create automated workflows using a visual drag-and-drop interface. Users can define triggers, conditions, and actions to automate repetitive tasks like status updates, notifications, and assignment routing.

The system supports complex branching logic, parallel execution paths, and custom webhook integrations. A real-time preview mode lets users test workflows before deploying them.

The GraphQL API provides a flexible query layer that allows the frontend to fetch exactly the data it needs, reducing payload sizes by 60% compared to the previous REST approach.
learnings: Building a visual programming interface is a UX challenge as much as a technical one. We went through 5 iterations of the drag-and-drop interaction model before finding one that felt intuitive. The biggest lesson: invest heavily in the undo/redo system early — users experiment freely when they know they can always go back.

name: AccessiCheck
pitch: An AI-powered accessibility auditing tool that goes beyond WCAG compliance to evaluate real-world usability.
description:
AccessiCheck combines traditional WCAG testing with AI-powered analysis to provide nuanced accessibility feedback. While standard tools check for code-level compliance, AccessiCheck evaluates the actual user experience for people with different abilities.

The tool uses Puppeteer to render pages, then applies computer vision models to analyze visual hierarchy, contrast patterns, and interactive element discoverability. An LLM generates human-readable recommendations with priority rankings.

AccessiCheck can audit entire sites by crawling sitemaps and generates comprehensive reports with before/after comparisons for remediated issues.
learnings: Accessibility is about people, not checklists. The most valuable feedback we got was from users with actual disabilities who tested our tool. Many WCAG-compliant sites are still unusable in practice. Our approach of combining automated testing with AI-powered UX analysis bridges that gap.

name: EventNexus
pitch: A high-throughput event processing system for real-time customer experience personalization.
description:
EventNexus is a backend system that processes millions of customer events per hour to enable real-time personalization across Adobe Experience Cloud products. The system uses Apache Kafka for event streaming, with custom partitioning strategies optimized for customer-level event ordering.

A Redis-based feature store maintains up-to-date customer profiles that can be queried in under 5ms, enabling real-time decisioning for ad targeting, content recommendations, and journey orchestration.

The gRPC API layer provides low-latency access for downstream services, with circuit breaker patterns and graceful degradation to ensure reliability under load.
learnings: Building for scale changes everything — patterns that work for 100 requests/second break at 100,000. We learned the hard way that premature optimization is bad, but premature architecture decisions are worse. Design for 10x your expected load from day one.

name: ContentIQ
pitch: An ML-powered content recommendation engine that predicts optimal content for each customer segment.
description:
ContentIQ uses transformer-based models to analyze content attributes and customer behavior patterns, generating personalized content recommendations that outperform rule-based systems by 23% on engagement metrics.

The system features a two-stage architecture: an offline training pipeline built on Apache Spark that processes historical interaction data, and a real-time inference service using optimized PyTorch models served via FastAPI.

A key innovation is the 'content embedding space' that maps both content items and user preferences into a shared vector space, enabling semantic matching that captures nuanced relationships beyond simple categorical filtering.
learnings: ML models are only as good as their training data — we spent 40% of our time on data cleaning and feature engineering, which felt boring but had the biggest impact on model performance. Also, a simple model with clean data beats a complex model with messy data every time.

name: InsightLens
pitch: A natural language querying interface that lets marketers ask data questions in plain English.
description:
InsightLens translates natural language questions into SQL queries, executes them against marketing analytics databases, and presents results as interactive visualizations. Non-technical marketers can ask questions like 'What was our best performing campaign in Q3?' without writing a single line of SQL.

The system uses LangChain to orchestrate a multi-step reasoning pipeline: understanding intent, mapping to database schema, generating SQL, validating results, and formatting responses with appropriate chart types.

InsightLens includes guardrails to prevent destructive queries, handles ambiguous questions by asking clarifying follow-ups, and maintains conversation context for multi-turn analytical sessions.
learnings: LLM-powered applications need extensive prompt engineering and guardrails. Our first prototype generated valid SQL only 60% of the time. By adding schema descriptions, few-shot examples, and a validation layer, we got to 94%. The lesson: LLMs are powerful but need careful orchestration.

name: SpectrumKit
pitch: A mobile-first component library implementing Adobe Spectrum design patterns for React Native.
description:
SpectrumKit brings Adobe's Spectrum design system to React Native with a comprehensive library of 30+ components. Each component supports theming, accessibility, and platform-adaptive behavior across iOS and Android.

The library features automatic Figma-to-code synchronization using the Figma API, ensuring that design tokens stay in sync between design files and implementation. A custom Storybook setup provides interactive documentation with live previews on both platforms.

Performance was a key focus — all components use optimized rendering patterns and native animations where possible, achieving 60fps interactions even on mid-range Android devices.
learnings: Building a design system is 20% building components and 80% building consensus. We learned that documentation and developer experience matter more than the components themselves. If engineers can't easily discover and use your components, they'll build their own.

name: VoiceOfUser
pitch: A sentiment analysis platform that aggregates and analyzes customer feedback across all touchpoints.
description:
VoiceOfUser aggregates customer feedback from support tickets, app reviews, social media, and NPS surveys into a unified sentiment analysis dashboard. The platform uses fine-tuned BERT models to classify sentiment, extract key themes, and identify emerging issues before they escalate.

The Elasticsearch backend enables real-time search across millions of feedback entries, with custom aggregation queries that power trend analysis and comparative visualizations.

A key feature is the 'Insight Alerts' system that automatically detects sentiment shifts and notifies product teams via Slack, enabling proactive response to customer concerns.
learnings: Sentiment analysis is surprisingly nuanced — sarcasm, cultural context, and domain-specific language all trip up generic models. Fine-tuning on Adobe-specific feedback data improved our accuracy by 15%. The big lesson: off-the-shelf ML models are starting points, not solutions.

name: TestPilot
pitch: An intelligent test generation and management platform for Workfront's microservice architecture.
description:
TestPilot automates the creation of integration tests for Workfront's complex microservice ecosystem. The platform analyzes API contracts and service dependencies to generate comprehensive test suites that cover common scenarios, edge cases, and failure modes.

A Docker-based test environment manager spins up isolated service instances for each test run, ensuring reliable and reproducible results. The React dashboard provides real-time test execution monitoring with detailed failure diagnostics.

TestPilot reduced the time to create new integration tests by 70% and caught 15 critical bugs that manual testing had missed.
learnings: Testing microservices is fundamentally different from testing monoliths. Service dependencies, network latency, and data consistency issues are the real challenges, not the test logic itself. Our biggest win was building the environment manager — reliable tests require reliable environments.

name: DeployGuard
pitch: A deployment safety system with automated canary analysis and instant rollback capabilities.
description:
DeployGuard adds intelligent deployment safety to the CI/CD pipeline. It manages canary deployments by gradually routing traffic to new versions while continuously monitoring error rates, latency percentiles, and business metrics.

The system uses statistical analysis to automatically detect anomalies in canary metrics and triggers instant rollback when degradations are detected. A Grafana dashboard provides real-time visibility into deployment health.

DeployGuard reduced deployment-related incidents by 80% in the teams that adopted it, and its automated rollback capability typically responds within 30 seconds of detecting an issue.
learnings: Deployment automation is about trust — teams won't use a system they don't trust. We spent significant time on the anomaly detection algorithm to minimize false positives, because one false rollback erodes confidence more than ten successful ones build it.

name: MotionLab
pitch: An interactive motion design playground for prototyping and sharing UI animations.
description:
MotionLab is a web-based playground where designers and developers can prototype, refine, and share UI animations. It provides a visual timeline editor for creating complex animation sequences, with real-time preview and code export.

The platform supports both CSS animations and Lottie files, with a conversion pipeline that translates between formats. A community gallery lets users share and remix each other's animations.

MotionLab generates production-ready code snippets in React (Framer Motion), CSS, and Lottie JSON, making it easy to go from prototype to implementation.
learnings: Building creative tools requires a different design approach — you need to give users enough structure to be productive but enough freedom to be creative. We learned that constraints actually enhance creativity when they're well-designed.

name: DocuBridge
pitch: An internal documentation platform that auto-generates API docs and connects knowledge across teams.
description:
DocuBridge solves the 'documentation rot' problem by automatically generating and updating API documentation from source code. It scans repositories for API endpoints, extracts types and descriptions, and generates interactive documentation pages.

The platform uses LLM-powered analysis to create human-readable explanations, code examples, and migration guides. A knowledge graph connects related APIs and concepts across teams, making it easy to discover relevant documentation.

DocuBridge integrates with GitHub PRs to flag documentation gaps when APIs change, ensuring docs stay current with the codebase.
learnings: Documentation is a product, not a chore. We learned that the key to keeping docs updated is removing friction from the process. Auto-generation handles 80% of the work, and making the remaining 20% easy to contribute is what makes the system sustainable.

name: BrandPulse
pitch: A brand consistency monitoring tool that tracks Adobe's visual identity across digital touchpoints.
description:
BrandPulse monitors Adobe's brand consistency across websites, social media, partner sites, and marketing materials. It uses computer vision to detect logo usage, color palette adherence, typography consistency, and layout patterns.

The D3.js-powered dashboard visualizes brand health metrics over time, with drill-down capabilities to inspect individual violations. Teams can set custom brand guidelines and receive automated alerts when consistency drops below thresholds.

The tool processed 10,000+ web pages during its evaluation period and identified 340+ brand inconsistencies that had gone unnoticed.
learnings: Computer vision for brand analysis is more challenging than it seems — logos on different backgrounds, responsive layouts, and design variations all require robust detection algorithms. We learned that combining rule-based checks with ML models gives the best results.

name: ComponentRadar
pitch: A design system adoption tracker that measures component usage and identifies custom overrides.
description:
ComponentRadar scans codebases to measure design system component adoption rates. It uses AST parsing to identify component usage, detect custom overrides, and surface opportunities for standardization.

The dashboard shows adoption trends over time, highlights teams with low adoption, and identifies the most commonly overridden components — signals that the design system may need to evolve.

ComponentRadar helped the Workfront team increase Spectrum component adoption from 62% to 84% by making adoption gaps visible and actionable.
learnings: Measuring component adoption sounds simple but gets complex fast — what counts as 'using' a component? We had to handle wrapper components, styled overrides, and partial usage. The key insight: metrics drive behavior, so choose what you measure very carefully.

name: SmartCrop
pitch: An intelligent image cropping service that uses ML to find the optimal crop for any aspect ratio.
description:
SmartCrop uses a combination of saliency detection, face detection, and aesthetic scoring to automatically determine the optimal crop region for any target aspect ratio. Unlike simple center-crop approaches, SmartCrop preserves the most important content in the image.

The model was trained on a dataset of professionally cropped images from Adobe Stock, learning the compositional preferences of expert photographers. It processes images in under 200ms, making it suitable for real-time applications.

SmartCrop is being evaluated for integration into Adobe Express and Adobe Experience Manager for automated asset adaptation.
learnings: Image cropping is subjective — what looks 'good' varies by context, culture, and use case. Training on professional examples helped, but the real breakthrough was adding user feedback loops. ML models that learn from their users continuously improve.

name: DevPortal CLI
pitch: A developer CLI that streamlines common workflows across Adobe's engineering toolchain.
description:
DevPortal CLI unifies access to Adobe's internal developer tools through a single command-line interface. Engineers can manage repositories, trigger deployments, query monitoring systems, and access documentation — all without leaving the terminal.

The CLI uses gRPC to communicate with backend services, providing fast and type-safe interactions. Plugin architecture allows teams to extend the CLI with custom commands for their specific workflows.

Within three weeks of launch, DevPortal CLI was adopted by 200+ engineers across the organization, reducing context-switching and improving developer productivity.
learnings: Developer tools live or die by their UX. We obsessed over command naming, error messages, and output formatting. The key lesson: study how developers actually work (shell history, aliases, common patterns) and design your CLI to fit into their existing workflows, not replace them.
